note: Expectation matrix for the 21-class mutation benchmark. `should_reject` is the AUTHORED intent, written before looking at results; `run.py` reports what actually happened and computes undocumented acceptance separately from acceptance that the design itself explains.

semantics.open: no key supplied: the seal's public key is read out of the package under test, so a signature proves internal consistency only (`trust_level=unanchored`).
semantics.pinned: public key supplied out-of-band (--pubkey), so key substitution is detectable.
semantics.head-pinned: pinned key AND a checkpoint head supplied out-of-band (--expect-head), so rollback to an older self-consistent package is detectable.

metric: undocumented_accept_rate = accepted cases that are NOT explained by an observation channel the mode lacks. This is the number that matters; the raw acceptance rate is reported beside it so the two can never be confused.

by_design_reason.M17: key substitution needs a key from outside the package; open mode has none.
by_design_reason.M20: a whole-package rollback is self-consistent and correctly signed; without a head observed outside the package there is nothing to compare against.
